translations.literal: Also called the lesser great divisor.
translations.idiomatic: Also called the lesser great divisor.

sentences.zh: 木精曰歲星，合率四千一百六萬三千八百八十九。

translations.literal: The essence of Wood is called the Year Star; its conjunction rate is forty-one million sixty-three thousand eight hundred eighty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: The essence of Wood is Jupiter; its conjunction rate is 41,063,889.

sentences.zh: 火精曰熒惑，合率八千二十九萬七千九百二十六。

translations.literal: The essence of Fire is called the Sparkling Deluder; its conjunction rate is eighty million two hundred ninety-seven thousand nine hundred twenty-six.
translations.idiomatic: The essence of Fire is Mars; its conjunction rate is 80,297,926.

sentences.zh: 土精曰鎮星，合率三千八百九十二萬五千四百一十三。

translations.literal: The essence of Earth is called the Queller Star; its conjunction rate is thirty-eight million nine hundred twenty-five thousand four hundred thirteen.
translations.idiomatic: The essence of Earth is Saturn; its conjunction rate is 38,925,413.

sentences.zh: 金精曰太白，合率六千一十一萬九千六百五十五。

translations.literal: The essence of Metal is called the Great White; its conjunction rate is sixty million one hundred nineteen thousand six hundred fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: The essence of Metal is Venus; its conjunction rate is 60,119,655.

sentences.zh: 水精曰辰星，合率一千一百九十三萬一千一百二十五。

translations.literal: The essence of Water is called the Chronogram Star; its conjunction rate is eleven million nine hundred thirty-one thousand one hundred twenty-five.
translations.idiomatic: The essence of Water is Mercury; its conjunction rate is 11,931,125.

sentences.zh: 張賓所創之曆既行，劉孝孫與冀州秀才劉焯，並稱其失，言學無師法，刻食不中，所駁凡有六條：其一雲，何承天不知分閏之有失，而用十九年之七閏。

translations.literal: After the calendar created by Zhang Bin was put into use, Liu Xiaosun and the Ji Province scholar Liu Chuo both declared its errors, saying its learning had no master and its eclipse predictions missed the mark; their objections numbered six in all: First, they said He Chengtian did not know the error in distributing intercalary months and used seven intercalations in nineteen years.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhang Bin's calendar was adopted, Liu Xiaosun and the Ji Province scholar Liu Chuo both challenged its errors, declaring that its methods lacked proper foundation and its eclipse predictions missed the mark. They raised six objections. First: He Chengtian did not recognize the error in distributing intercalary months and used the seven-intercalation-in-nineteen-years rule.

sentences.zh: 其二雲，賓等不解宿度之差改，而冬至之日守常度。

translations.literal: Second, they said Bin and the others did not understand the changing discrepancy in lodge degrees and kept the winter solstice at a fixed degree.
translations.idiomatic: Second: Zhang Bin and his colleagues did not account for the shifting discrepancy in lodge degrees and kept the winter solstice at a fixed position.

sentences.zh: 其三雲，連珠合璧，七曜須同，乃以五星別元。

translations.literal: Third, they said that when strung pearls and joined jades align, the seven luminaries must share the same origin, yet they set separate origins for the five planets.
translations.idiomatic: Third: when the heavenly markers align, the seven luminaries must share a single origin, yet they assigned separate origins to the five planets.

sentences.zh: 其四雲，賓等唯知日氣餘分恰盡而為立元之法，不知日月不合，不成朔旦冬至。

translations.literal: Fourth, they said Bin and the others knew only that when the sun's qi remainder was exactly exhausted one could establish the origin method, but did not know that when sun and moon fail to conjoin, new-moon dawn and winter solstice cannot be fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth: Zhang Bin and his colleagues knew only that when the solar qi remainder is exactly exhausted one may set the origin, but did not grasp that without sun-moon conjunction, new-moon dawn and winter solstice cannot be fixed.

sentences.zh: 其五雲，賓等但守立元定法，不須明有進退。

translations.literal: Fifth, they said Bin and the others merely adhered to the fixed method of establishing the origin and need not clarify advance and retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth: Zhang Bin and his colleagues merely clung to a fixed origin method and did not account for advance and retreat.

sentences.zh: 其六雲，賓等唯識轉加大餘二十九以為朔，不解取日月合會准以為定。

translations.literal: Sixth, they said Bin and the others knew only to add the rotating large remainder of twenty-nine to obtain the new moon, but did not understand taking sun-moon conjunction as the standard for fixing it.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth: Zhang Bin and his colleagues knew only to add the rotating large remainder of twenty-nine to obtain the new moon, but did not understand using sun-moon conjunction as the basis for fixing it.

sentences.zh: 此六事微妙，歷數大綱，聖賢之通術，而暉未曉此，實管窺之謂也。

translations.literal: These six matters are subtle; they are the great outline of calendrical reckoning and the common method of sages—yet Hui did not understand them; this is truly what is called viewing through a bamboo tube.
translations.idiomatic: These six points are subtle matters—the great framework of calendrical science and the common method of sages—yet Liu Hui did not grasp them. This was indeed viewing the heavens through a bamboo tube.

sentences.zh: 若乃驗影定氣，何氏所優，賓等推測，去之彌遠。

translations.literal: As for verifying shadows to fix the qi, the He family was superior; Bin and the others' deductions departed ever further.
translations.idiomatic: In verifying shadows to fix the seasonal nodes, He's method was superior; Zhang Bin's deductions strayed ever further.

sentences.zh: 合朔順天，何氏所劣，賓等依據，循彼迷蹤。

translations.literal: In conjunction with Heaven at new moon, the He family was inferior; Bin and the others followed and traced their mistaken tracks.
translations.idiomatic: In aligning new moons with Heaven, He's method was weaker; Zhang Bin followed and traced that mistaken path.

sentences.zh: 蓋是失其菁華，得其糠粃者也。

translations.literal: In general they lost the essence and got the chaff.
translations.idiomatic: In short, they discarded the essence and kept the chaff.

sentences.zh: 又雲，魏明帝時，有尚書郎楊偉，修《景初曆》，乃上表立義，駁難前非，雲：「加時後天，食不在朔。

translations.literal: They also said that in the time of Emperor Ming of Wei, the Secretariat Gentleman Yang Wei revised the Jingchu Calendar and submitted a memorial setting forth principles, refuting earlier errors, saying: "The hour of occurrence lags behind Heaven, and the eclipse is not on the new moon."
translations.idiomatic: They also noted that under Emperor Ming of Wei, Secretariat Gentleman Yang Wei revised the Jingchu Calendar and submitted a memorial refuting earlier errors: "The hour of occurrence lags behind Heaven, and the eclipse does not fall on the new moon."

sentences.zh: 」然觀楊偉之意，故以食朔為真，未能詳之而制其法。

translations.literal: Close quotation. Yet examining Yang Wei's intent, he therefore took eclipse-on-new-moon as true but was unable to explain it in detail and formulate the method.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wei's intent was to treat eclipse-on-new-moon as the standard, but he could not fully explain it or formulate the method.

sentences.zh: 至宋元嘉中，何承天著曆，其上表雲：「月行不定，或有遲疾，合朔月食，不在朔望，亦非曆之意也。

translations.literal: In the Yuanjia era of Liu Song, He Chengtian compiled a calendar; his submitted memorial said: "The moon's motion is not fixed; sometimes it is slow or fast. Conjunction and lunar eclipse do not fall on new or full moon—this also is not the calendar's intent."
translations.idiomatic: In the Liu Song's Yuanjia era, He Chengtian compiled a calendar whose submitted memorial stated: "The moon's motion is not uniform; it may be slow or fast. Conjunction and lunar eclipse do not always fall on new or full moon—this too departs from the calendar's intent."

sentences.zh: 」然承天本意，欲立合朔之術，遭皮延宗飾非致難，故事不得行。

translations.literal: Close quotation. Yet Chengtian's original intent was to establish a method for conjunction, but he encountered Pi Yanzong's embellishment of error and provocation of difficulty, so the matter could not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: He Chengtian's original intent was to establish a conjunction method, but Pi Yanzong's obstruction prevented it from being implemented.

sentences.zh: 至後魏獻帝時，有龍宜弟複修延興之曆，又上表雲：「日食不在朔，而習之不廢，據《春秋》書食，乃天之驗朔也。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Xian of Later Wei, Long Yidi again revised the Yanxing calendar and submitted a memorial saying: "Solar eclipses do not fall on the new moon, yet the practice is not abandoned; according to the Spring and Autumn Annals' records of eclipses, Heaven verifies the new moon."
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xian of Later Wei, Long Yidi again revised the Yanxing calendar and submitted a memorial: "Solar eclipses do not fall on the new moon, yet the practice persists; according to the Spring and Autumn Annals' eclipse records, Heaven verifies the new moon."

sentences.zh: 」此三人者，前代善曆，皆有其意，未正其書。

translations.literal: Close quotation. These three men were skilled calendrists of former ages; all had the right idea but did not correct their writings.
translations.idiomatic: These three were skilled calendrists of earlier ages; each had the right insight but failed to correct their written methods.

sentences.zh: 但歷數所重，唯在朔氣。

translations.literal: Yet what calendrical reckoning most values is only the new moon and the qi.
translations.idiomatic: Yet calendrical reckoning values above all the new moon and the seasonal nodes.

sentences.zh: 朔為朝會之首，氣為生長之端，朔有告餼之文，氣有郊迎之典，故孔子命曆而定朔旦冬至，以為將來之範。

translations.literal: The new moon is the head of court assemblies; the qi is the beginning of growth; the new moon has the rite of announcing provisions, and the qi has the ceremony of suburban greeting—therefore Confucius fixed the calendar and established new-moon dawn and winter solstice as the model for the future.
translations.idiomatic: The new moon heads the court assembly; the seasonal node marks the start of growth. The new moon has its rite of announcing provisions; the node has its suburban greeting ceremony. Confucius therefore fixed the calendar and established new-moon dawn and winter solstice as the model for posterity.

sentences.zh: 今孝孫曆法，並按明文，以月行遲疾定其合朔，欲今食必在朔，不在晦、二之日也。

translations.literal: Now Xiaosun's calendrical method follows the explicit texts, using the moon's slow and fast motion to fix conjunction, wishing that eclipses must fall on the new moon and not on the last day or second day.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiaosun's calendar follows the explicit texts, using the moon's anomalistic motion to fix conjunction so that eclipses fall on the new moon, not on the last or second day of the month.

sentences.zh: 縱使頻月一小、三大，得天之統。

translations.literal: Even if frequently one small month and three large months occur in a month, this attains Heaven's unity.
translations.idiomatic: Even if months frequently alternate one short and three long, this accords with Heaven's unity.

sentences.zh: 大抵其法有三，今列之雲。

translations.literal: In general its method has three parts; they are listed below.
translations.idiomatic: The method has three parts in all, listed below.

sentences.zh: 第一，勘日食證恆在朔。

translations.literal: First: verify that solar eclipses constantly fall on the new moon.
translations.idiomatic: First: verify that solar eclipses always fall on the new moon.

sentences.zh: 引《詩》雲：「十月之交，朔日辛卯，日有食之。

translations.literal: It cites the Odes: "At the crossing of the tenth month, on the xinmao day of the new moon, the sun was eclipsed."
translations.idiomatic: It cites the Odes: "At the crossing of the tenth month, on the xinmao day of the new moon, the sun was eclipsed."

sentences.zh: 」今以甲子元曆術推算，符合不差。

translations.literal: Close quotation. Now calculating by the Jiazi Origin Calendar method, the match is exact without discrepancy.
translations.idiomatic: Calculated by the Jiazi Origin Calendar, the match is exact.

sentences.zh: 《春秋經》書日食三十五。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals records thirty-five solar eclipses.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals records thirty-five solar eclipses.

sentences.zh: 二十七日食，經書有朔，推與甲子元曆不差。

translations.literal: Twenty-seven eclipses—the classic records a new moon; calculation with the Jiazi Origin Calendar matches without discrepancy.
translations.idiomatic: Of twenty-seven eclipses where the classic records a new moon, calculation with the Jiazi Origin Calendar matches exactly.

sentences.zh: 八食，經書並無朔字。

translations.literal: Eight eclipses—the classic records no new-moon character.
translations.idiomatic: Eight eclipses are recorded without the new-moon character.

sentences.zh: 《左氏傳》雲：「不書朔，官失之也。

translations.literal: The Zuo Commentary says: "Not recording the new moon—an error of the officials."
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo Commentary says: "Failure to record the new moon was an error of the officials."

sentences.zh: 」《公羊傳》雲：「不言朔者，食二日也。

translations.literal: Close quotation. The Gongyang Commentary says: "Not stating the new moon—the eclipse was on the second day."
translations.idiomatic: The Gongyang Commentary says: "Failure to state the new moon means the eclipse was on the second day."

sentences.zh: 「《谷梁傳》雲：「不言朔者，食晦也。

translations.literal: Close quotation. The Guliang Commentary says: "Not stating the new moon—the eclipse was on the last day."
translations.idiomatic: The Guliang Commentary says: "Failure to state the new moon means the eclipse was on the last day."

sentences.zh: 」今以甲子元曆推算，俱是朔日。

translations.literal: Close quotation. Now calculating by the Jiazi Origin Calendar, all are new-moon days.
translations.idiomatic: Calculated by the Jiazi Origin Calendar, all eight fall on new-moon days.

sentences.zh: 丘明受經夫子，于理尤詳，《公羊》、《谷梁》皆臆說也。

translations.literal: Qiu Ming received the classic from the Master and is especially detailed in principle; the Gongyang and Guliang are both speculative interpretations.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Qiuming received the classic directly from Confucius and is far more reliable; the Gongyang and Guliang commentaries are speculative interpretations.

sentences.zh: 《春秋左氏》隱公三年二月己巳，日有食之。

translations.literal: The Zuo Commentary of the Spring and Autumn Annals, third year of Duke Yin, second month, day jisi—there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo Commentary, Duke Yin year 3, second month, day jisi: a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 推合己巳朔

translations.literal: Calculation matches conjunction on jisi new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Calculation confirms conjunction on the jisi-day new moon.

sentences.zh: 莊公十八年春三月，日有食之。

translations.literal: Duke Zhuang, eighteenth year, spring, third month—there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Zhuang, year 18, spring, third month: a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 推合壬子朔

translations.literal: Calculation matches conjunction on renzi new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Calculation confirms conjunction on the renzi-day new moon.

sentences.zh: 僖公十二年三月庚午，日有食之。

translations.literal: Duke Xi, twelfth year, third month, day gengwu—there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Xi, year 12, third month, day gengwu: a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 推合庚午朔

translations.literal: Calculation matches conjunction on gengwu new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Calculation confirms conjunction on the gengwu-day new moon.

sentences.zh: 十五年夏五月，日有食之。

translations.literal: Fifteenth year, summer, fifth month—there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Year 15, summer, fifth month: a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 推合癸未朔

translations.literal: Calculation matches conjunction on guiwei new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Calculation confirms conjunction on the guiwei-day new moon.

sentences.zh: 襄公十五年秋八月丁巳，日有食之。

translations.literal: Duke Xiang, fifteenth year, autumn, eighth month, day dingsi—there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Xiang, year 15, autumn, eighth month, day dingsi: a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 推合丁巳朔

translations.literal: Calculation matches conjunction on dingsi new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Calculation confirms conjunction on the dingsi-day new moon.

sentences.zh: 前、後漢及魏、晉四代所記日食，朔、晦及先晦，都合一百八十一，今以甲子元曆術推之，併合朔日而食。

translations.literal: Solar eclipses recorded by the Former and Later Han and the Wei and Jin over four dynasties, on new moon, last day, and day before last day—in all one hundred eighty-one; now calculating by the Jiazi Origin Calendar method, all match new-moon-day eclipses.
translations.idiomatic: The 181 solar eclipses recorded by the Former and Later Han, Wei, and Jin—whether dated to new moon, last day, or day before last—all calculate as new-moon eclipses under the Jiazi Origin Calendar.

sentences.zh: 前漢合有四十五食。

translations.literal: Former Han in all had forty-five eclipses.
translations.idiomatic: The Former Han recorded forty-five eclipses in all.

sentences.zh: 三食並先晦一日，三十二食並皆晦日，十食並是朔日

translations.literal: Three eclipses were all one day before the last day; thirty-two eclipses were all on the last day; ten eclipses were all on the new-moon day.
translations.idiomatic: Three fell one day before the last day; thirty-two on the last day; ten on the new-moon day.

sentences.zh: 後漢合有七十四食。

translations.literal: Later Han in all had seventy-four eclipses.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Han recorded seventy-four eclipses in all.

sentences.zh: 三十七食並皆晦日，三十七食並皆朔日

translations.literal: Thirty-seven eclipses were all on the last day; thirty-seven eclipses were all on the new-moon day.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-seven fell on the last day; thirty-seven on the new-moon day.

sentences.zh: 魏合有十四食。

translations.literal: Wei in all had fourteen eclipses.
translations.idiomatic: Wei recorded fourteen eclipses in all.

sentences.zh: 四食並皆晦日，十食並皆朔日

translations.literal: Four eclipses were all on the last day; ten eclipses were all on the new-moon day.
translations.idiomatic: Four fell on the last day; ten on the new-moon day.

sentences.zh: 晉合有四十八食。

translations.literal: Jin in all had forty-eight eclipses.
translations.idiomatic: Jin recorded forty-eight eclipses in all.

sentences.zh: 二十五食並皆晦日，二十三食並皆朔日

translations.literal: Twenty-five eclipses were all on the last day; twenty-three eclipses were all on the new-moon day.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-five fell on the last day; twenty-three on the new-moon day.

sentences.zh: 第二，勘度差變驗。

translations.literal: Second: verify the changing discrepancy in degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Second: verify the changing discrepancy in celestial degrees.

sentences.zh: 第三，勘氣影長驗。

translations.literal: Third: verify by qi and shadow length.
translations.idiomatic: Third: verify by seasonal nodes and gnomon shadow length.

sentences.zh: 《春秋緯命曆序》雲：「魯僖公五年正月壬子朔旦冬至。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Apocrypha, Calendar Sequence Command, says: "In the fifth year of Duke Xi of Lu, first month, day renzi, new-moon dawn, winter solstice."
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Apocrypha, Calendar Sequence Command, states: "Duke Xi of Lu, year 5, first month, day renzi, new-moon dawn, winter solstice."

sentences.zh: 」今以甲子元曆術推算，得合不差。

translations.literal: Close quotation. Now calculating by the Jiazi Origin Calendar method, the match is exact without discrepancy.
translations.idiomatic: Calculated by the Jiazi Origin Calendar, the match is exact.

sentences.zh: 《宋書》元嘉十年，何承天以土圭測影，知冬至已差三日。

translations.literal: The History of Song: in the tenth year of Yuanjia, He Chengtian measured shadows with the earth gnomon and knew the winter solstice had already differed by three days.
translations.idiomatic: The History of Song records that in Yuanjia 10, He Chengtian measured shadows with an earth gnomon and found the winter solstice had already drifted by three days.

sentences.zh: 詔使付外考驗，起元嘉十三年為始，畢元嘉二十年，八年之中，冬至之日恆與影長之日差校三日。

translations.literal: An edict ordered it sent out for verification, beginning from the thirteenth year of Yuanjia and ending in the twentieth year of Yuanjia; within eight years, on winter solstice days it constantly differed from the longest-shadow days by three days upon comparison.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered external verification from Yuanjia 13 through Yuanjia 20; over eight years, winter solstice consistently differed from the longest-shadow day by three days.

sentences.zh: 今以甲子元曆術推算，但是冬至之日恆與影長之符合不差。

translations.literal: Now calculating by the Jiazi Origin Calendar method, on every winter solstice day it constantly matches the longest-shadow day without discrepancy.
translations.idiomatic: Calculated by the Jiazi Origin Calendar, every winter solstice matches the longest-shadow day exactly.

sentences.zh: 詳之如左：

translations.literal: The details are as follows:
translations.idiomatic: The details are as follows:

sentences.zh: 十三年丙子，

translations.literal: Thirteenth year (bingzi),
translations.idiomatic: Thirteenth year (bingzi),

sentences.zh: 天正十八日曆注冬至，

translations.literal: On the eighteenth day of the celestial first month the calendar notes winter solstice,
translations.idiomatic: Celestial first month, day 18: calendar notes winter solstice;

sentences.zh: 十五日影長，

translations.literal: On the fifteenth day the shadow was longest,
translations.idiomatic: Day 15: longest shadow;

sentences.zh: 即是今曆冬至日。

translations.literal: This is the winter solstice day in the present calendar.
translations.idiomatic: This matches the present calendar's winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 十四年丁丑，

translations.literal: Fourteenth year (dingchou),
translations.idiomatic: Fourteenth year (dingchou),

sentences.zh: 天正二十九日曆注冬至，

translations.literal: On the twenty-ninth day of the celestial first month the calendar notes winter solstice,
translations.idiomatic: Celestial first month, day 29: calendar notes winter solstice;

sentences.zh: 二十六日影長，

translations.literal: On the twenty-sixth day the shadow was longest,
translations.idiomatic: Day 26: longest shadow;

sentences.zh: 即是今曆冬至日。

translations.literal: This is the winter solstice day in the present calendar.
translations.idiomatic: This matches the present calendar's winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 十五年戊寅，

translations.literal: Fifteenth year (wuyin),
translations.idiomatic: Fifteenth year (wuyin),

sentences.zh: 天正十一日曆注冬至，

translations.literal: On the eleventh day of the celestial first month the calendar notes winter solstice,
translations.idiomatic: Celestial first month, day 11: calendar notes winter solstice;

sentences.zh: 陰，無影可驗，

translations.literal: Overcast; no shadow could be verified,
translations.idiomatic: Overcast—no shadow could be measured;

sentences.zh: 今曆八日冬至。

translations.literal: The present calendar has winter solstice on the eighth day.
translations.idiomatic: Present calendar: winter solstice on day 8.

sentences.zh: 十六年己卯，

translations.literal: Sixteenth year (jimao),
translations.idiomatic: Sixteenth year (jimao),

sentences.zh: 天正二十一日曆注冬至，

translations.literal: On the twenty-first day of the celestial first month the calendar notes winter solstice,
translations.idiomatic: Celestial first month, day 21: calendar notes winter solstice;

sentences.zh: 十八日影長，

translations.literal: On the eighteenth day the shadow was longest,
translations.idiomatic: Day 18: longest shadow;

sentences.zh: 即是今曆冬至日。

translations.literal: This is the winter solstice day in the present calendar.
translations.idiomatic: This matches the present calendar's winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 十七年庚辰，

translations.literal: Seventeenth year (gengchen),
translations.idiomatic: Seventeenth year (gengchen),

sentences.zh: 天正二日曆注冬至，

translations.literal: On the second day of the celestial first month the calendar notes winter solstice,
translations.idiomatic: Celestial first month, day 2: calendar notes winter solstice;

sentences.zh: 十月二十九日影長，

translations.literal: On the twenty-ninth day the shadow was longest,
translations.idiomatic: Day 29: longest shadow;

sentences.zh: 即是今曆冬至日。

translations.literal: This is the winter solstice day in the present calendar.
translations.idiomatic: This matches the present calendar's winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 十八年辛巳，

translations.literal: Eighteenth year (xinsi),
translations.idiomatic: Eighteenth year (xinsi),

sentences.zh: 天正十三日曆注冬至，

translations.literal: On the thirteenth day of the celestial first month the calendar notes winter solstice,
translations.idiomatic: Celestial first month, day 13: calendar notes winter solstice;

sentences.zh: 十日影長，

translations.literal: On the tenth day the shadow was longest,
translations.idiomatic: Day 10: longest shadow;

sentences.zh: 即是今曆冬至日。

translations.literal: This is the winter solstice day in the present calendar.
translations.idiomatic: This matches the present calendar's winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 十九年壬午，

translations.literal: Nineteenth year (renwu),
translations.idiomatic: Nineteenth year (renwu),

sentences.zh: 天正二十九日曆注冬至，

translations.literal: On the twenty-ninth day of the celestial first month the calendar notes winter solstice,
translations.idiomatic: Celestial first month, day 29: calendar notes winter solstice;

sentences.zh: 陰，無影可驗，

translations.literal: Overcast; no shadow could be verified,
translations.idiomatic: Overcast—no shadow could be measured;

sentences.zh: 今曆二十二日冬至。

translations.literal: The present calendar has winter solstice on the twenty-second day.
translations.idiomatic: Present calendar: winter solstice on day 22.

sentences.zh: 二十年癸未，

translations.literal: Twentieth year (guiwei),
translations.idiomatic: Twentieth year (guiwei),

sentences.zh: 天正六日曆注冬至，

translations.literal: On the sixth day of the celestial first month the calendar notes winter solstice,
translations.idiomatic: Celestial first month, day 6: calendar notes winter solstice;

sentences.zh: 三日影長，

translations.literal: On the third day the shadow was longest,
translations.idiomatic: Day 3: longest shadow;

sentences.zh: 即是今曆冬至日。

translations.literal: This is the winter solstice day in the present calendar.
translations.idiomatic: This matches the present calendar's winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 于時新曆初頒，賓有寵于高祖，劉暉附會之，被升為太史令。

translations.literal: At that time the new calendar had just been promulgated; Bin enjoyed Gaozu's favor, and Liu Hui attached himself to him and was promoted to Grand Astrologer.
translations.idiomatic: The new calendar had just been promulgated. Zhang Bin enjoyed Gaozu's favor, and Liu Hui attached himself to Bin and was promoted to Grand Astrologer.

sentences.zh: 二人協議，共短孝孫，言其非毀天曆，率意迂怪，焯又妄相扶證，惑亂時人。

translations.literal: The two men joined in agreement to disparage Xiaosun together, saying he slandered and destroyed the celestial calendar, willfully making perverse and strange claims; Chuo also falsely supported and verified this, confusing the people of the time.
translations.idiomatic: The two men colluded to attack Liu Xiaosun, accusing him of slandering the official calendar and making willfully eccentric claims. Liu Chuo falsely backed them, sowing confusion among scholars of the day.

sentences.zh: 孝孫、焯等，竟以他事斥罷。

translations.literal: Xiaosun, Chuo, and the others were ultimately dismissed on other charges.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiaosun, Liu Chuo, and their allies were ultimately dismissed on other pretexts.

sentences.zh: 後賓死，孝孫為掖縣丞，委官入京，又上，前後為劉暉所詰，事寢不行。

translations.literal: Later, when Bin died, Xiaosun was Assistant Magistrate of Ye County; he resigned his office and entered the capital, submitting memorials again and again, but was repeatedly challenged by Liu Hui, and the matter was abandoned without implementation.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Bin's death, Liu Xiaosun, then Assistant Magistrate of Ye County, resigned and went to the capital to submit his calendar again. Liu Hui repeatedly blocked him, and the proposal went nowhere.

sentences.zh: 仍留孝孫直太史，累年不調，寓宿觀台。

translations.literal: Xiaosun was still retained as a direct appointee of the Grand Astrologer's office, unrewarded with promotion for many years, lodging at the Observational Platform.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiaosun remained attached to the Grand Astrologer's office as a direct appointee, unrewarded for years, lodging at the Observational Platform.

sentences.zh: 乃抱其書，弟子輿櫬，來詣闕下，伏而慟哭。

translations.literal: He then embraced his writings; his disciples carried his coffin and came to the palace gates, prostrating themselves and wailing.
translations.idiomatic: He then brought his writings; his disciples carried his coffin to the palace gates, where he prostrated himself and wept.

sentences.zh: 執法拘以奏之，高祖異焉，以問國子祭酒何妥。

translations.literal: The law officers detained him and reported this; Gaozu was struck by it and asked the Director of the Imperial Academy, He Tuo.
translations.idiomatic: Law officers detained him and reported to the throne. Gaozu was moved and consulted Director of the Imperial Academy He Tuo.

sentences.zh: 妥言其善，即日擢授大都督，遣與賓曆比校短長。

translations.literal: Tuo said it was good; that very day Xiaosun was promoted to Grand Commander and sent to compare his calendar with Bin's for strengths and weaknesses.
translations.idiomatic: He Tuo endorsed the work, and Liu Xiaosun was immediately promoted to Grand Commander and ordered to compare his calendar with Zhang Bin's.

sentences.zh: 先是信都人張胄玄，以算術直太史，久未知名。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhang Zhouxuan of Xindu, skilled in computation, served directly under the Grand Astrologer and had long been unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zhang Zhouxuan of Xindu, skilled in computation, had served under the Grand Astrologer in obscurity for years.

sentences.zh: 至是與孝孫共短賓曆，異論鋒起，久之不定。

translations.literal: At this time he joined Xiaosun in disparaging Bin's calendar; conflicting opinions flared up and long remained unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Now he joined Liu Xiaosun in attacking Zhang Bin's calendar. Conflicting opinions multiplied and remained unresolved for a long time.

sentences.zh: 至十四年七月，上令參問日食事。

translations.literal: By the seventh month of the fourteenth year, the emperor ordered an inquiry into solar eclipses.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Kaihuang 14, the emperor ordered an inquiry into solar eclipse predictions.

sentences.zh: 楊素等奏：「太史凡奏日食二十有五，唯一晦三朔，依克而食，尚不得其時，又不知所起，他皆無驗。

translations.literal: Yang Su and others memorialized: "The Grand Astrologer in all submitted twenty-five solar eclipses; only one on the last day and three on new moons, according to prediction and eclipse, still missed the correct time and did not know where they began; the rest were all unverified."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su and others reported: "The Grand Astrologer's office submitted twenty-five eclipse predictions. Only four—one on the last day and three on new moons—even roughly matched the event, and those missed the correct hour and origin. The rest failed entirely."

sentences.zh: 胄玄所克，前後妙衷，時起分數，合如符契。

translations.literal: Zhouxuan's predictions, before and after, were subtly accurate; the times and fractional parts matched like tally and seal.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhouxuan's predictions were consistently accurate; the times and fractional parts matched like tally and seal.

sentences.zh: 孝孫所克，驗亦過半。

translations.literal: Xiaosun's predictions were verified in more than half the cases.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiaosun's predictions were verified in more than half the cases.

sentences.zh: 」於是高祖引孝孫、胄玄等，親自勞徠。

translations.literal: Close quotation. Thereupon Gaozu summoned Xiaosun, Zhouxuan, and the others and personally received and comforted them.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu then summoned Liu Xiaosun, Zhang Zhouxuan, and the others and personally received them.

sentences.zh: 孝孫因請先斬劉暉，乃可定曆。

translations.literal: Xiaosun therefore requested that Liu Hui be executed first before the calendar could be fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiaosun then demanded that Liu Hui be executed before the calendar could be fixed.

sentences.zh: 高祖不懌，又罷之。

translations.literal: Gaozu was displeased and dismissed him again.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was displeased and dismissed him again.

sentences.zh: 俄而孝孫卒，楊素、牛弘等傷惜之，又薦胄玄。

translations.literal: Soon Xiaosun died; Yang Su, Niu Hong, and others grieved for him and again recommended Zhouxuan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiaosun soon died. Yang Su, Niu Hong, and others mourned him and again recommended Zhang Zhouxuan.

sentences.zh: 上召見之，胄玄因言日長影短之事，高祖大悅，賞賜甚厚，令與參定新術。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned and received him; Zhouxuan spoke on the matter of longer days and shorter shadows, and Gaozu was greatly pleased, richly rewarding him and ordering him to participate in fixing the new method.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Zhang Zhouxuan, who spoke on the lengthening of days and shortening of shadows. Gaozu was greatly pleased, richly rewarded him, and ordered him to help fix the new calendar.

sentences.zh: 劉焯聞胄玄進用，又增損孝孫曆法，更名《七曜新術》，以奏之。

translations.literal: When Chuo heard that Zhouxuan had been promoted, he again added to and reduced Xiaosun's calendrical method, renaming it the "New Method of the Seven Luminaries," and submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Chuo learned of Zhang Zhouxuan's promotion, he revised Liu Xiaosun's calendar, renamed it the New Method of the Seven Luminaries, and submitted it.

sentences.zh: 與胄玄之法，頗相乖爽，袁充與胄玄害之。

translations.literal: Compared with Zhouxuan's method, it was largely at variance; Yuan Chong and Zhouxuan harmed him.
translations.idiomatic: It diverged significantly from Zhang Zhouxuan's method. Yuan Chong and Zhang Zhouxuan worked against him.

sentences.zh: 焯又罷。

translations.literal: Chuo was again dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chuo was dismissed again.

sentences.zh: 至十七年，胄玄曆成，奏之。

translations.literal: By the seventeenth year, Zhouxuan's calendar was completed and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: By Kaihuang 17, Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar was complete and submitted.

sentences.zh: 上付楊素等校其短長。

translations.literal: The emperor entrusted it to Yang Su and others to compare its strengths and weaknesses.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor entrusted it to Yang Su and others to evaluate its merits.

sentences.zh: 劉暉與國子助教王頍等執舊曆術，迭相駁難，與司曆劉宜援據古史影等，駁胄玄雲：

translations.literal: Liu Hui and the Academy Assistant Instructor Wang Yi and others held to the old calendrical method, mutually refuting and challenging; together with Calendar Officer Liu Yi they drew on ancient histories and shadow records to refute Zhouxuan, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hui and Academy Assistant Instructor Wang Yi defended the old calendar, trading refutations with Zhang Zhouxuan. Calendar Officer Liu Yi drew on ancient histories and shadow records to challenge him, stating:

sentences.zh: 《命曆序》僖公五年天正壬子朔旦日至，《左氏傳》僖公五年正月辛亥朔日南至。

translations.literal: The Calendar Sequence Command: fifth year of Duke Xi, celestial first month, day renzi, new-moon dawn, sun reaches extreme. The Zuo Commentary: fifth year of Duke Xi, first month, day xinhai, new moon, sun reaches south extreme.
translations.idiomatic: The Calendar Sequence Command records Duke Xi's fifth year, celestial first month, day renzi, new-moon dawn, winter solstice. The Zuo Commentary records Duke Xi's fifth year, first month, day xinhai, new moon, winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 張賓曆，天正壬子朔冬至，合《命曆序》，差《傳》一日。

translations.literal: Zhang Bin's calendar: celestial first month, day renzi new moon, winter solstice—matches the Calendar Sequence Command, differs from the Commentary by one day.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin's calendar: celestial first month, renzi-day new moon, winter solstice—matches the Calendar Sequence Command, differs from the Zuo Commentary by one day.

sentences.zh: 張胄玄曆，天正壬子朔，合《命曆序》，差《傳》一日；

translations.literal: Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar: celestial first month, day renzi new moon—matches the Calendar Sequence Command, differs from the Commentary by one day;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar: celestial first month, renzi-day new moon—matches the Calendar Sequence Command, differs from the Zuo Commentary by one day;

sentences.zh: 三日甲寅冬至，差《命曆序》二日，差《傳》三日。

translations.literal: Third day, day jiayin, winter solstice—differs from the Calendar Sequence Command by two days, from the Commentary by three days.
translations.idiomatic: Third day, jiayin, winter solstice—off by two days from the Calendar Sequence Command, three from the Zuo Commentary.

sentences.zh: 成公十二年，《命曆序》天正辛卯朔旦日至。

translations.literal: Twelfth year of Duke Cheng: the Calendar Sequence Command has celestial first month, day xinmao, new-moon dawn, sun reaches extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Cheng, year 12: the Calendar Sequence Command records celestial first month, xinmao-day new-moon dawn, winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 張賓曆，天正辛卯朔冬至，合《命曆序》。

translations.literal: Zhang Bin's calendar: celestial first month, day xinmao new moon, winter solstice—matches the Calendar Sequence Command.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin's calendar: celestial first month, xinmao-day new moon, winter solstice—matches the Calendar Sequence Command.

sentences.zh: 張胄玄曆，天正辛卯朔，合《命曆序》；

translations.literal: Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar: celestial first month, day xinmao new moon—matches the Calendar Sequence Command;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar: celestial first month, xinmao-day new moon—matches the Calendar Sequence Command;

sentences.zh: 二日壬辰冬至，差《命曆序》一日。

translations.literal: Second day, day renchen, winter solstice—differs from the Calendar Sequence Command by one day.
translations.idiomatic: Second day, renchen, winter solstice—off by one day from the Calendar Sequence Command.

sentences.zh: 昭公二十年，《春秋左氏傳》二月己丑朔日南至，准《命曆序》庚寅朔旦日至。

translations.literal: Twentieth year of Duke Zhao: the Zuo Commentary of the Spring and Autumn Annals, second month, day jichou new moon, sun reaches south extreme; according to the Calendar Sequence Command, day gengyin new-moon dawn, sun reaches extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Zhao, year 20: the Zuo Commentary records second month, jichou-day new moon, winter solstice; the Calendar Sequence Command records gengyin-day new-moon dawn, winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 張賓曆，天正庚寅朔冬至，併合《命曆序》，差《傳》一日。

translations.literal: Zhang Bin's calendar: celestial first month, day gengyin new moon, winter solstice—matches the Calendar Sequence Command together, differs from the Commentary by one day.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin's calendar: celestial first month, gengyin-day new moon, winter solstice—matches the Calendar Sequence Command, differs from the Zuo Commentary by one day.

sentences.zh: 張胄玄曆，天正庚寅朔，合《命曆序》，差《傳》一日；

translations.literal: Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar: celestial first month, day gengyin new moon—matches the Calendar Sequence Command, differs from the Commentary by one day;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar: celestial first month, gengyin-day new moon—matches the Calendar Sequence Command, differs from the Zuo Commentary by one day;

sentences.zh: 二日辛卯冬至，差《命曆序》一日，差《傳》二日。

translations.literal: Second day, day xinmao, winter solstice—differs from the Calendar Sequence Command by one day, from the Commentary by two days.
translations.idiomatic: Second day, xinmao, winter solstice—off by one day from the Calendar Sequence Command, two from the Zuo Commentary.

sentences.zh: 宜案《命曆序》及《春秋左氏傳》，並閏餘盡之歲，皆須朔旦冬至。

translations.literal: Yi finds that according to the Calendar Sequence Command and the Zuo Commentary of the Spring and Autumn Annals, in all years when the intercalary remainder is exhausted, new-moon dawn and winter solstice are required.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi argues that according to the Calendar Sequence Command and the Zuo Commentary, in every year when the intercalary remainder is exhausted, new-moon dawn and winter solstice must coincide.

sentences.zh: 若依《命曆序》勘《春秋》三十七食，合處至多；

translations.literal: If one verifies the thirty-seven eclipses of the Spring and Autumn Annals according to the Calendar Sequence Command, the matches are very numerous;
translations.idiomatic: Checking the Spring and Autumn Annals' thirty-seven eclipses against the Calendar Sequence Command yields numerous matches;

sentences.zh: 若依《左傳》，合者至少，是以知《傳》為錯。

translations.literal: if according to the Zuo Commentary, the matches are very few—therefore one knows the Commentary is in error.
translations.idiomatic: checking against the Zuo Commentary yields very few—proving the Commentary is in error.

sentences.zh: 今張胄玄信情置閏，《命曆序》及《傳》氣朔並差。

translations.literal: Now Zhang Zhouxuan arbitrarily sets intercalation according to his own judgment; the qi and new moons of the Calendar Sequence Command and the Commentary all differ.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhouxuan arbitrarily sets intercalation by personal judgment; the seasonal nodes and new moons diverge from both the Calendar Sequence Command and the Zuo Commentary.

sentences.zh: 又宋元嘉冬至影有七，張賓曆合者五，差者二，亦在前一日。

translations.literal: Also in Yuanjia of Liu Song there were seven winter-solstice shadow records; Zhang Bin's calendar matched five and missed two, both one day early.
translations.idiomatic: Of seven Yuanjia-era winter-solstice shadow records, Zhang Bin's calendar matched five and missed two—both one day early.

sentences.zh: 張胄玄曆合者三，差者四，在後一日。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar matched three and missed four, all one day late.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar matched three and missed four—all one day late.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十二年十一月甲寅朔，十五日戊辰冬至，日影長。

translations.literal: Twelfth year of Yuanjia, eleventh month, day jiayin new moon; fifteenth day, day wuchen, winter solstice; the sun's shadow was long.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjia 12, eleventh month, jiayin-day new moon; fifteenth day, wuchen, winter solstice; longest shadow.

sentences.zh: 張賓曆合戊辰冬至，張胄玄曆己巳冬至，差後一日。

translations.literal: Zhang Bin's calendar matches wuchen winter solstice; Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar has jisi winter solstice, one day late.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin's calendar: wuchen winter solstice. Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar: jisi winter solstice—one day late.

sentences.zh: 十三年十一月己酉朔，二十六日甲戌冬至，日影長。

translations.literal: Thirteenth year, eleventh month, day jiyou new moon; twenty-sixth day, day jiaxu, winter solstice; the sun's shadow was long.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjia 13, eleventh month, jiyou-day new moon; twenty-sixth day, jiaxu, winter solstice; longest shadow.

sentences.zh: 張賓曆癸酉冬至，差前一日，張胄玄曆合甲戌冬至。

translations.literal: Zhang Bin's calendar has guiyou winter solstice, one day early; Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar matches jiaxu winter solstice.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin's calendar: guiyou winter solstice—one day early. Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar: jiaxu winter solstice—correct.

sentences.zh: 十五年十一月丁卯朔，十八日甲申冬至，日影長。

translations.literal: Fifteenth year, eleventh month, day dingmao new moon; eighteenth day, day jiashen, winter solstice; the sun's shadow was long.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjia 15, eleventh month, dingmao-day new moon; eighteenth day, jiashen, winter solstice; longest shadow.

sentences.zh: 二曆併合甲申冬至。

translations.literal: Both calendars together match jiashen winter solstice.
translations.idiomatic: Both calendars agree on jiashen winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 十六年十一月辛酉朔，二十九日己丑冬至，日影長。

translations.literal: Sixteenth year, eleventh month, day xinyou new moon; twenty-ninth day, day jichou, winter solstice; the sun's shadow was long.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjia 16, eleventh month, xinyou-day new moon; twenty-ninth day, jichou, winter solstice; longest shadow.

sentences.zh: 張賓曆合己丑冬至，張胄玄曆庚寅冬至，差後一日。

translations.literal: Zhang Bin's calendar matches jichou winter solstice; Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar has gengyin winter solstice, one day late.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin's calendar: jichou winter solstice. Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar: gengyin winter solstice—one day late.

sentences.zh: 十七年十一月乙酉朔，十日甲午冬至，日影長。

translations.literal: Seventeenth year, eleventh month, day yiyou new moon; tenth day, day jiawu, winter solstice; the sun's shadow was long.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjia 17, eleventh month, yiyou-day new moon; tenth day, jiawu, winter solstice; longest shadow.

sentences.zh: 張賓曆合甲午冬至，張胄玄曆乙未冬至，差後一日。

translations.literal: Zhang Bin's calendar matches jiawu winter solstice; Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar has yiwu winter solstice, one day late.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin's calendar: jiawu winter solstice. Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar: yiwu winter solstice—one day late.

sentences.zh: 十八年十一月己卯朔，二十一日己亥冬至，日影長。

translations.literal: Eighteenth year, eleventh month, day jimao new moon; twenty-first day, day jihai, winter solstice; the sun's shadow was long.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjia 18, eleventh month, jimao-day new moon; twenty-first day, jihai, winter solstice; longest shadow.

sentences.zh: 張賓曆合己亥冬至，張胄玄曆庚子冬至，差後一日。

translations.literal: Zhang Bin's calendar matches jihai winter solstice; Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar has gengzi winter solstice, one day late.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin's calendar: jihai winter solstice. Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar: gengzi winter solstice—one day late.

sentences.zh: 十九年十一月癸卯朔，三日乙巳冬至，影長。

translations.literal: Nineteenth year, eleventh month, day guimao new moon; third day, day yisi, winter solstice; shadow long.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjia 19, eleventh month, guimao-day new moon; third day, yisi, winter solstice; longest shadow.

sentences.zh: 張賓曆甲辰冬至，差前一日，張胄玄曆合乙巳冬至。

translations.literal: Zhang Bin's calendar has jiachen winter solstice, one day early; Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar matches yisi winter solstice.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin's calendar: jiachen winter solstice—one day early. Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar: yisi winter solstice—correct.

sentences.zh: 又周從天和元年丙戌至開皇十五年乙卯，合得冬夏至日影一十四。

translations.literal: Also from the first year of Tianhe, bingxu, of Zhou down to the fifteenth year of Kaihuang, yimao, there are fourteen winter and summer solstice shadow records in all.
translations.idiomatic: From Northern Zhou's Tianhe 1 (bingxu) through Sui's Kaihuang 15 (yimao), fourteen winter and summer solstice shadow records are available.

sentences.zh: 張賓曆合得者十，差者四，三差前一日，一差後一日。

translations.literal: Zhang Bin's calendar matched ten and missed four—three one day early, one one day late.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin's calendar matched ten and missed four—three one day early, one one day late.

sentences.zh: 張胄玄曆合者五，差者九，八差後一日，一差前一日。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar matched five and missed nine—eight one day late, one one day early.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar matched five and missed nine—eight one day late, one one day early.

sentences.zh: 天和二年十一月戊戌朔，三日庚子冬至，日影長。

translations.literal: Second year of Tianhe, eleventh month, day wuxu new moon; third day, day gengzi, winter solstice; the sun's shadow was long.
translations.idiomatic: Tianhe 2, eleventh month, wuxu-day new moon; third day, gengzi, winter solstice; longest shadow.

sentences.zh: 張賓曆合庚子冬至，張胄玄曆辛丑冬至，差後一日。

translations.literal: Zhang Bin's calendar matches gengzi winter solstice; Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar has xinchou winter solstice, one day late.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin's calendar: gengzi winter solstice. Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar: xinchou winter solstice—one day late.

sentences.zh: 三年十一月壬辰朔，十四日乙巳冬至，日影長。

translations.literal: Third year, eleventh month, day renchen new moon; fourteenth day, day yisi, winter solstice; the sun's shadow was long.
translations.idiomatic: Tianhe 3, eleventh month, renchen-day new moon; fourteenth day, yisi, winter solstice; longest shadow.

sentences.zh: 張賓曆合乙巳冬至，張胄玄曆丙午冬至，差後一日。

translations.literal: Zhang Bin's calendar matches yisi winter solstice; Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar has bingwu winter solstice, one day late.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin's calendar: yisi winter solstice. Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar: bingwu winter solstice—one day late.

sentences.zh: 建德元年十一月己亥朔，二十九日丁卯冬至，日影長。

translations.literal: First year of Jiande, eleventh month, day jihai new moon; twenty-ninth day, day dingmao, winter solstice; the sun's shadow was long.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande 1, eleventh month, jihai-day new moon; twenty-ninth day, dingmao, winter solstice; longest shadow.

sentences.zh: 張賓曆丙寅冬至，差前一日，張胄玄曆合丁卯冬至。

translations.literal: Zhang Bin's calendar has bingyin winter solstice, one day early; Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar matches dingmao winter solstice.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin's calendar: bingyin winter solstice—one day early. Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar: dingmao winter solstice—correct.

sentences.zh: 二年五月丙寅朔，三日戊辰夏至，日影短。

translations.literal: Second year, fifth month, day bingyin new moon; third day, day wuchen, summer solstice; the sun's shadow was short.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande 2, fifth month, bingyin-day new moon; third day, wuchen, summer solstice; shortest shadow.

sentences.zh: 張賓曆己巳夏至，差後一日，張胄玄曆庚午夏至，差後二日。

translations.literal: Zhang Bin's calendar has jisi summer solstice, one day late; Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar has gengwu summer solstice, two days late.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin's calendar: jisi summer solstice—one day late. Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar: gengwu summer solstice—two days late.

sentences.zh: 三年十一月戊午朔，二十日丁丑冬至，日影長。

translations.literal: Year 3, eleventh month, wu-wu-day new moon;, day 20, ding-chou, Winter Solstice, longest shadow.
translations.idiomatic: Year 3, eleventh month, wu-wu-day new moon;, day 20, ding-chou, Winter Solstice, longest shadow.

sentences.zh: 張賓曆合丁丑冬至，張胄玄曆戊寅冬至，差後一日。

translations.literal: Zhang Bin's calendar matches ding-chou winter solstice; Zhang Zhouxuan's calendarwu-yin winter solstice; —one day late.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin's calendar matches ding-chou winter solstice; Zhang Zhouxuan's calendarwu-yin winter solstice; —one day late.

sentences.zh: 六年十一月庚午朔，二十三日壬辰冬至，日影長。

translations.literal: Year 6, eleventh month, geng-wu-day new moon;, day 23, ren-chen, Winter Solstice, longest shadow.
translations.idiomatic: Year 6, eleventh month, geng-wu-day new moon;, day 23, ren-chen, Winter Solstice, longest shadow.

sentences.zh: 張賓曆合壬辰冬至，張胄玄曆癸巳冬至，差後一日。

translations.literal: Zhang Bin's calendar matches ren-chen winter solstice; Zhang Zhouxuan's calendargui-si winter solstice; —one day late.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin's calendar matches ren-chen winter solstice; Zhang Zhouxuan's calendargui-si winter solstice; —one day late.

sentences.zh: 宣政元年十一月甲午朔，五日戊戌冬至，日影長。

translations.literal: Xuanzheng Year 1, eleventh month, jia-wu-day new moon;, day 5, wu-xu, winter solstice, longest shadow.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzheng Year 1, eleventh month, jia-wu-day new moon;, day 5, wu-xu, winter solstice, longest shadow.

sentences.zh: 兩曆併合戊戌冬至。

translations.literal: Both calendars together match wuxu winter solstice.
translations.idiomatic: Both calendars agree on wuxu winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 開皇四年十一月己未朔，十一日己巳冬至，日影長。

translations.literal: KaihuangYear 4, eleventh month, ji-wei-day new moon;, day 11, ji-si, Winter Solstice, longest shadow.
translations.idiomatic: KaihuangYear 4, eleventh month, ji-wei-day new moon;, day 11, ji-si, Winter Solstice, longest shadow.

sentences.zh: 張賓曆合己巳冬至，張胄玄曆庚午冬至，差後一日。

translations.literal: Zhang Bin's calendar matches ji-zi winter solstice; Zhang Zhouxuan's calendargeng-zi winter solstice; —one day late.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin's calendar matches ji-zi winter solstice; Zhang Zhouxuan's calendargeng-zi winter solstice; —one day late.

sentences.zh: 五年十一月甲寅朔，二十二日乙亥冬至，日影長。

translations.literal: Year 5, eleventh month, jia-yin-day new moon;, day 22, yi-hai, Winter Solstice, longest shadow.
translations.idiomatic: Year 5, eleventh month, jia-yin-day new moon;, day 22, yi-hai, Winter Solstice, longest shadow.

sentences.zh: 張賓曆甲戌冬至，差前一日，張胄玄曆合庚辰冬至。

translations.literal: Zhang Bin's calendar has jiaxu winter solstice, one day early; Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar matches gengchen winter solstice.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin's calendar: jiaxu winter solstice—one day early. Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar: gengchen winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 七年五月乙亥朔，九日癸未夏至，日影短。

translations.literal: Year 7, fifth month, yi-hai-day new moon;, day 9, gui-wei, Summer Solstice, shortest shadow.
translations.idiomatic: Year 7, fifth month, yi-hai-day new moon;, day 9, gui-wei, Summer Solstice, shortest shadow.

sentences.zh: 張賓曆壬午夏至，差前一日，張胄玄曆合癸未夏至。

translations.literal: Summer Solstice,, Summer Solstice.
translations.idiomatic: Summer Solstice,, Summer Solstice.

sentences.zh: 十一月壬申朔，十四日乙酉冬至，日影長。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, ren-shen-day new moon;, day 14, yi-you, Winter Solstice, longest shadow.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month, ren-shen-day new moon;, day 14, yi-you, Winter Solstice, longest shadow.

sentences.zh: 張賓曆合乙酉冬至，張胄玄曆丙戌冬至，差後一日。

translations.literal: Zhang Bin's calendar matches yi-you winter solstice; Zhang Zhouxuan's calendarbing-xu winter solstice; —one day late.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin's calendar matches yi-you winter solstice; Zhang Zhouxuan's calendarbing-xu winter solstice; —one day late.

sentences.zh: 十一年十一月己卯朔，二十八日丙午冬至，日影長。

translations.literal: Year 11, eleventh month, ji-mao-day new moon;, day 28, bing-wu, Winter Solstice, longest shadow.
translations.idiomatic: Year 11, eleventh month, ji-mao-day new moon;, day 28, bing-wu, Winter Solstice, longest shadow.

sentences.zh: 張賓曆合丙午冬至，張胄玄曆丁未冬至，差後一日。

translations.literal: Zhang Bin's calendar matches bing-wu winter solstice; Zhang Zhouxuan's calendarding-wei winter solstice; —one day late.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin's calendar matches bing-wu winter solstice; Zhang Zhouxuan's calendarding-wei winter solstice; —one day late.

sentences.zh: 十四年十一月辛酉朔旦冬至。

translations.literal: Fourteenth year, eleventh month, day xinyou, new-moon dawn, winter solstice.
translations.idiomatic: Kaihuang 14, eleventh month, xinyou-day new-moon dawn, winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 張賓曆合十一月辛酉朔旦冬至，張胄玄曆十一月辛酉朔，二日壬戌冬至，差後一日。

translations.literal: Zhang Bin's calendar matches eleventh month, day xinyou, new-moon dawn, winter solstice; Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar has eleventh month, day xinyou new moon; second day, day renchen, winter solstice, one day late.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin's calendar: eleventh month, xinyou-day new-moon dawn, winter solstice. Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar: xinyou-day new moon; renchen day 2, winter solstice—one day late.

sentences.zh: 建德四年四月大、乙酉朔，三十日甲寅，月晨見東方。

translations.literal: Fourth year of Jiande, fourth month long, day yiyou new moon; thirtieth day, day jiayin—the moon was seen in the morning in the east.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande 4, fourth month (long), yiyou-day new moon; thirtieth day, jiayin—the moon was visible in the morning eastern sky.

sentences.zh: 張賓曆四月大、乙酉朔，三十日甲寅，月晨見東方，張胄玄曆四月小、乙酉朔，五月大，甲寅朔，月晨見東方。

translations.literal: Zhang Bin's calendar: fourth month long, day yiyou new moon; thirtieth day, day jiayin—the moon was seen in the morning in the east. Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar: fourth month short, day yiyou new moon; fifth month long, day jiayin new moon—the moon was seen in the morning in the east.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin's calendar: fourth month (long), yiyou new moon; day 30, jiayin—morning moon in the east. Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar: fourth month (short), yiyou new moon; fifth month (long), jiayin new moon—morning moon in the east.

sentences.zh: 宜案影極長為冬至，影極短為夏至，二至自古史分可勘者二十四，其二十一有影，三有至日無影。

translations.literal: Yi finds that the longest shadow marks winter solstice and the shortest shadow marks summer solstice; of twenty-four solstices verifiable from ancient histories, twenty-one have shadow records and three have solstice days without shadows.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi argues that the longest shadow marks winter solstice and the shortest marks summer solstice. Of twenty-four solstices verifiable from ancient records, twenty-one have shadow data and three record the solstice day without shadow measurements.

sentences.zh: 見行曆合一十八，差者六。

translations.literal: The calendar in use matched eighteen; six differed.
translations.idiomatic: The calendar then in use matched eighteen cases; six did not.

sentences.zh: 旅騎尉張胄玄曆合者八，差者一十六，二差後二日，一十四差後一日。

translations.literal: Cavalry Commandant Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar matched eight; sixteen differed—two two days late, fourteen one day late.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar matched eight cases and missed sixteen—two by two days, fourteen by one day.

sentences.zh: 又開皇四年，在洛州測冬至影，與京師二處，進退絲毫不差。

translations.literal: Also in Kaihuang 4, winter solstice shadows were measured at Luoyang and the capital; at both places the advance and retreat matched to the slightest hair without discrepancy.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang 4, winter solstice shadows measured at Luoyang and the capital agreed to the finest precision at both locations.

sentences.zh: 周天和已來案驗並在後。

translations.literal: From Tianhe of Zhou onward, verified cases all fall later.
translations.idiomatic: From Northern Zhou's Tianhe era onward, all verified cases fall one day late.

sentences.zh: 更檢得建德四年，晦朔東見；

translations.literal: Further checking found Jiande 4, last day of month, new moon, morning sighting in the east;
translations.idiomatic: Further review found Jiande 4: on the last day of the month at new moon, the moon was sighted in the morning east;

sentences.zh: 張胄玄曆，五月朔日，月晨見東方。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar: fifth month new-moon day—the moon was seen in the morning in the east.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar: fifth-month new-moon day—the moon visible in the morning east.

sentences.zh: 今十七年，張賓曆閏七月，張胄玄曆閏五月。

translations.literal: Also examining year seventeen: Zhang Bin's calendar has intercalary seventh month; Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar has intercalary fifth month.
translations.idiomatic: Examining Kaihuang 17: Zhang Bin's calendar places the intercalary month in the seventh month; Zhang Zhouxuan's in the fifth.

sentences.zh: 又審至以定閏，胄玄曆至既不當，故知置閏必乖。

translations.literal: Also, since intercalation is determined by the solstice, and Zhouxuan's calendar misses the solstice, one knows his intercalary placement must be wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Since intercalation should be determined by the solstice, and Zhang Zhouxuan's solstice is wrong, his intercalary placement must be incorrect.

sentences.zh: 見行曆四月、五月頻大，張胄玄曆九月、十月頻大，為胄玄朔弱，頻大在後晨，故朔日殘月晨見東方。

translations.literal: The calendar in use frequently has long fourth and fifth months; Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar frequently has long ninth and tenth months—because Zhouxuan's new moons are weak, with frequent long months in later mornings, hence on new-moon day the waning moon is seen in the morning in the east.
translations.idiomatic: The official calendar frequently assigns long fourth and fifth months; Zhang Zhouxuan's frequently assigns long ninth and tenth months. His new-moon reckoning is weak, producing long months in later morning hours—hence the waning moon appears in the eastern morning sky on new-moon day.

sentences.zh: 宜又案開皇四年十二月十五日癸卯，依曆月行在鬼三度，時加酉，月在卯上，食十五分之九，虧起西北。

translations.literal: Yi also cites Kaihuang 4, twelfth month, fifteenth day, day guimao: according to the calendar the moon was at three degrees of Ghost; hour added you; the moon was above mao; eclipse nine fifteenths; obscuration began northwest.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi also cites Kaihuang 4, twelfth month, day 15 (guimao): per the calendar the moon was at 3° Ghost; hour you; moon above mao; eclipse magnitude 9/15; obscuration began in the northwest.

sentences.zh: 今伺候，一更一籌起食東北角，十五分之十，至四籌還生，至二更一籌複滿。

translations.literal: Now observed: at the first watch, first tally, obscuration began at the northeast corner, ten fifteenths; by the fourth tally it was restored; by the second watch, first tally, fully restored.
translations.idiomatic: Observed: at the first watch, first tally, obscuration began at the northeast limb, magnitude 10/15; restored by the fourth tally; fully restored by the second watch, first tally.

sentences.zh: 五年六月三十日，依曆太陽虧，日在七星六度，加時在午少強上，食十五分之一半強，虧起西南角。

translations.literal: Fifth year, sixth month, thirtieth day: according to the calendar the sun was eclipsed; the sun at six degrees of Seven Stars; hour of occurrence at wu slightly strong; eclipse one and a half fifteenths strong; obscuration began southwest corner.
translations.idiomatic: Kaihuang 5, sixth month, day 30: per the calendar, solar eclipse; sun at 6° Seven Stars; hour of occurrence mid-wu; magnitude 1.5/15; obscuration began at the southwest limb.

sentences.zh: 今伺候，日乃在午後六刻上始食，虧起西北角，十五分之六，至未後一刻還生，至五刻複滿。

translations.literal: Now observed: the sun began eclipsing after the sixth quarter of wu; obscuration began northwest corner, six fifteenths; restored after the first quarter of wei; fully restored by the fifth quarter.
translations.idiomatic: Observed: eclipse began after the sixth quarter-hour of wu; obscuration from the northwest, magnitude 6/15; restoration began after the first quarter of wei; full restoration by the fifth quarter.

sentences.zh: 六年六月十五日，依曆太陰虧，加時酉，在卯上，食十五分之九半弱，虧起西南，當其時陰雲不見月。

translations.literal: Sixth year, sixth month, fifteenth day: according to the calendar the moon was eclipsed; hour added you; above mao; eclipse nine and a half fifteenths weak; obscuration began southwest; at the time clouds hid the moon.
translations.idiomatic: Kaihuang 6, sixth month, day 15: per the calendar, lunar eclipse; hour you; moon above mao; magnitude 9.5/15; obscuration from the southwest; clouds obscured the moon at the time.

sentences.zh: 至辰巳，雲裡見月，已食三分之二，虧從東北，既還雲合。

translations.literal: By chen and si, the moon was seen through clouds, already two-thirds eclipsed; obscuration from the northeast; after totality clouds closed again.
translations.idiomatic: By chen-si hours the moon appeared through clouds, already two-thirds eclipsed from the northeast; after totality clouds closed again.

sentences.zh: 至巳午間稍生，至午後，雲裡暫見，已複滿。

translations.literal: By si-wu it slightly restored; by afternoon clouds briefly parted—the moon was fully restored.
translations.idiomatic: Restoration began around si-wu; by afternoon a break in the clouds showed the moon fully restored.

sentences.zh: 十月三十日丁丑，依曆太陽虧，日在斗九度，時加在辰少弱上，食十五分之九強，虧起東北角。

translations.literal: Tenth month, thirtieth day, day dingchou: according to the calendar the sun was eclipsed; the sun at nine degrees of Dipper; hour added at chen slightly weak; eclipse nine fifteenths strong; obscuration began northeast corner.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth month, day 30 (dingchou): per the calendar, solar eclipse; sun at 9° Dipper; hour chen slightly weak; magnitude 9/15; obscuration from the northeast.

sentences.zh: 今候所見，日出山一丈，辰二刻始食，虧起正西，食三分之二，辰後二刻始生，入巳時三刻上複滿。

translations.literal: Now observed: the sun one zhang above the mountains at rise; eclipse began at the second quarter of chen; obscuration from due west, two-thirds eclipsed; restoration began after the second quarter of chen; fully restored entering the third quarter of si.
translations.idiomatic: Observed: sun one zhang above the horizon at sunrise; eclipse began at chen 2; obscuration from the west, two-thirds magnitude; restoration after chen 2; full restoration by si 3.

sentences.zh: 十年三月十六日癸卯，依曆月行在氐七度，時加戌，月在辰太半上，食十五分之七半強，虧起東北。

translations.literal: Tenth year, third month, sixteenth day, day guimao: according to the calendar the moon at seven degrees of Di; hour added xu; moon above chen greatly past midpoint; eclipse seven and a half fifteenths strong; obscuration began northeast.
translations.idiomatic: Kaihuang 10, third month, day 16 (guimao): per the calendar moon at 7° Di; hour xu; moon well past chen; magnitude 7.5/15; obscuration from the northeast.

sentences.zh: 今候，月初出卯南，帶半食，出至辰初三分，可食二分許，漸生，辰未已複滿。

translations.literal: Now observed: the moon at month's first rising south of mao, half eclipsed; by the beginning of chen about two-thirds eclipsed; gradually restored; fully restored before wei.
translations.idiomatic: Observed: at first rising south of mao the moon was half eclipsed; by early chen about two-thirds; gradual restoration; fully restored before wei.

sentences.zh: 見行曆九月十六日庚子，月行在胃四度，時加醜，月在未半強上，食十分之三半強，虧起正東。

translations.literal: The calendar in use, ninth month, sixteenth day, day gengzi: moon at four degrees of Stomach; hour added chou; moon above wei half strong; eclipse three and a half tenths strong; obscuration began due east.
translations.idiomatic: Official calendar, ninth month, day 16 (gengzi): moon at 4° Stomach; hour chou; moon above wei; magnitude 3.5/10; obscuration from the east.

sentences.zh: 今伺候，月以午後二刻，食起正東，須臾如南，至未正上，食南畔五分之四，漸生，入申一刻半複滿。

translations.literal: Now observed: the moon at the second quarter after wu, eclipse began due east; shortly turning south; at the exact center of wei, four-fifths of the south limb eclipsed; gradually restored; fully restored entering the first and a half quarter of shen.
translations.idiomatic: Observed: eclipse began due east at the second quarter after wu; briefly turning south; at exact wei, four-fifths of the southern limb eclipsed; gradual restoration; full by shen 1.5.

sentences.zh: 十二年七月十五日己未，依曆月行在室七度，時加戌，月在辰太強上，食十五分之十二半弱，虧起西北。

translations.literal: Twelfth year, seventh month, fifteenth day, day jiwei: according to the calendar the moon at seven degrees of Room; hour added xu; moon above chen very strong; eclipse twelve and a half fifteenths weak; obscuration began northwest.
translations.idiomatic: Kaihuang 12, seventh month, day 15 (jiwei): per the calendar moon at 7° Room; hour xu; moon above chen; magnitude 12.5/15; obscuration from the northwest.

sentences.zh: 今伺候，一更三籌起西北上，食准三分之二強，與曆注同。

translations.literal: Now observed: at the first watch, third tally, obscuration began northwest; eclipse about two-thirds strong—matching the calendar note.
translations.idiomatic: Observed: at the first watch, third tally, obscuration began northwest at about two-thirds magnitude—matching the calendar prediction.

sentences.zh: 十三年七月十六日，依曆月在申半強上，食十五分之半弱，虧起西南。

translations.literal: Thirteenth year, seventh month, sixteenth day: according to the calendar the moon above shen half strong; eclipse half a fifteenth weak; obscuration began southwest.
translations.idiomatic: Kaihuang 13, seventh month, day 16: per the calendar moon above shen; magnitude 0.5/15; obscuration from the southwest.

sentences.zh: 十五日夜，從四更候月，五更一籌起東北上，食半強，入雲不見。

translations.literal: On the fifteenth night, watching from the fourth watch—the moon at the first tally of the fifth watch began northeast; half strong eclipsed; entered clouds and was not seen.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the 15th, watching from the fourth watch: at the fifth watch, first tally, obscuration began northeast at half magnitude; then lost in clouds.

sentences.zh: 十四年七月一日，依歷時加巳弱上，食十五分之十二半強。

translations.literal: Fourteenth year, seventh month, first day: according to the calendar hour added si weak; eclipse twelve and a half fifteenths strong.
translations.idiomatic: Kaihuang 14, seventh month, day 1: per the calendar, hour si weak; magnitude 12.5/15.

sentences.zh: 至未後三刻，日乃食，虧起西北，食半許，入雲不見，食頃暫見，猶未複生，因即雲鄣。

translations.literal: By the third quarter after wei the sun was eclipsed; obscuration began northwest; about half eclipsed; entered clouds; briefly seen during the eclipse but not yet restored; then cloud-covered.
translations.idiomatic: By wei 3 the sun was eclipsed from the northwest at about half magnitude; lost in clouds; briefly visible during totality but not yet restored; then obscured again.

sentences.zh: 十五年十一月十六日庚午，依曆月行在井十七度，時加亥，月在巳半上，食十五分之九半強，虧西北。

translations.literal: Fifteenth year, eleventh month, sixteenth day, day gengwu: according to the calendar the moon at seventeen degrees of Well; hour added hai; moon above si half; eclipse nine and a half fifteenths strong; obscuration northwest.
translations.idiomatic: Kaihuang 15, eleventh month, day 16 (gengwu): per the calendar moon at 17° Well; hour hai; moon above si; magnitude 9.5/15; obscuration northwest.

sentences.zh: 其夜一更四籌後，月在辰上起食，虧東南，至二更三籌，月在巳上，食三分之二許，漸生，至三更一籌，月在丙上，複滿。

translations.literal: That night after the first watch, fourth tally, the moon above chen began eclipsing; obscuration southeast; by the second watch, third tally, moon above si, about two-thirds eclipsed; gradually restored; by the third watch, first tally, moon above bing, fully restored.
translations.idiomatic: That night after the first watch, fourth tally: moon above chen, eclipse began southeast; by second watch, third tally, moon above si, about two-thirds; gradual restoration; by third watch, first tally, moon above bing, fully restored.

sentences.zh: 十六年十一月十六日乙丑，依曆月行在井十七度，時加醜，月在未太弱上，食十五分之十二半弱，虧起東南。

translations.literal: Sixteenth year, eleventh month, sixteenth day, day yichou: according to the calendar the moon at seventeen degrees of Well; hour added chou; moon above wei very weak; eclipse twelve and a half fifteenths weak; obscuration began southeast.
translations.idiomatic: Kaihuang 16, eleventh month, day 16 (yichou): per the calendar moon at 17° Well; hour chou; moon above wei; magnitude 12.5/15; obscuration from the southeast.

sentences.zh: 十五日夜伺候，至三更一籌，月在丙上，雲裡見，已食十五分之三許，虧起正東，至丁上，食既，後從東南生，至四更三籌，月在未末，複滿。

translations.literal: On the fifteenth night observed: by the third watch, first tally, moon above bing seen through clouds, already about three fifteenths eclipsed; obscuration began due east; at ding, totality; then restored from the southeast; by the fourth watch, third tally, moon at the end of wei, fully restored.
translations.idiomatic: Observed on the night of the 15th: by third watch, first tally, moon above bing seen through clouds, already about 3/15 eclipsed from the east; totality at ding; restoration from the southeast; by fourth watch, third tally, moon at end of wei, fully restored.

sentences.zh: 而胄玄不能盡中。

translations.literal: Yet Zhouxuan could not fully hit the mark.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zhang Zhouxuan could not fully hit the mark.

sentences.zh: 迭相駁難，高祖惑焉，逾時不決。

translations.literal: They mutually refuted and challenged; Gaozu was perplexed, and for a long time no decision was made.
translations.idiomatic: The parties traded refutations until Gaozu was perplexed and no decision was reached for a long time.

sentences.zh: 會通事舍人顏慜楚上書雲：「漢落下閎改《顓頊曆》作《太初曆》，雲後八百歲，此曆差一日。

translations.literal: Then Palace Attendant Yan Minting submitted a memorial, saying: "Under Han, Luoxia Hong revised the Zhuanxu Calendar to make the Taichu Calendar, saying that after eight hundred years this calendar would differ by one day."
translations.idiomatic: Then Palace Attendant Yan Minting submitted a memorial: "Under the Han, Luoxia Hong revised the Zhuanxu Calendar into the Taichu Calendar, declaring that after eight hundred years it would err by one day."

sentences.zh: 」語在胄玄傳。

translations.literal: The account is in Zhouxuan's biography.
translations.idiomatic: The account appears in Zhang Zhouxuan's biography.

sentences.zh: 高祖欲神其事，遂下詔曰：「朕應運受圖，君臨萬宇，思欲興複聖教，恢弘令典，上順天道，下授人時，搜揚海內，廣延術士。

translations.literal: Gaozu wished to make the matter miraculous and therefore issued an edict: "We have received the mandate and the chart, ruling the myriad realms, wishing to revive sage teaching and expand the great statutes, aligning above with the Way of Heaven and below granting the seasons to the people, searching within the seas and broadly extending to masters of technique."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu wished to invest the matter with portentous significance and issued an edict: "Having received the mandate, We rule the realm, seeking to revive sage teaching and expand the statutes—aligning with Heaven above and granting the seasons to the people below, searching far and wide for masters of calendrical science."

sentences.zh: 旅騎尉張胄玄，理思沉敏，術藝宏深，懷道白首，來上曆法。

translations.literal: Cavalry Commandant Zhang Zhouxuan—his reasoning deep and keen, his arts vast and profound, devoted to the Way until white-haired age—came to submit a calendar method.
translations.idiomatic: Cavalry Commandant Zhang Zhouxuan, deep of mind and vast in skill, devoted to the Way into old age, submitted his calendar method.

sentences.zh: 令與太史舊曆，並加勘審。

translations.literal: He was ordered together with the Grand Astrologer's old calendar jointly to examine and verify.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to compare his calendar jointly with the Grand Astrologer's existing system.

sentences.zh: 仰觀玄象，參驗璿璣，胄玄歷數與七曜符合，太史所行，乃多疏舛，群官博議，咸以胄玄為密。

translations.literal: Looking up to observe the dark images and verifying against the armillary sphere, Zhouxuan's reckoning matched the seven luminaries; what the Grand Astrologer practiced was largely coarse and erroneous; the officials' broad deliberation all judged Zhouxuan as precise.
translations.idiomatic: Observing the heavens and verifying against the armillary sphere, Zhang Zhouxuan's reckoning matched the seven luminaries, while the Grand Astrologer's system was largely erroneous. The assembled officials judged Zhang Zhouxuan's method the more precise.

sentences.zh: 太史令劉暉，司曆郭翟、劉宜，驍騎尉任悅，往經修造，致此乖謬。

translations.literal: Grand Astrologer Liu Hui, Calendar Officers Guo Di and Liu Yi, and Cavalry Commandant Ren Yue—having previously revised and created—caused these errors.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Astrologer Liu Hui, Calendar Officers Guo Di and Liu Yi, and Cavalry Commandant Ren Yue—who had previously devised the calendar—were responsible for these errors.

sentences.zh: 通直散騎常侍、領太史令庾季才，太史丞邢俊，司曆郭遠，曆博士蘇粲，曆助教傅俊、成珍等，既是職司，須審疏密。

translations.literal: Direct Palace Attendant and Grand Astrologer Yu Jicai, Assistant Grand Astrologer Xing Jun, Calendar Officer Guo Yuan, Calendar Erudite Su Can, and Calendar Assistant Instructors Fu Jun and Cheng Zhen—as they were officers of duty, had to examine density and sparsity.
translations.idiomatic: Direct Palace Attendant and Grand Astrologer Yu Jicai, Assistant Grand Astrologer Xing Jun, Calendar Officer Guo Yuan, and Erudites Su Can, Fu Jun, and Cheng Zhen—as calendrical officers—should have reviewed the system's accuracy.

sentences.zh: 遂虛行此曆，無所發明。

translations.literal: Yet they vainly allowed this calendar to be used without any contribution.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they allowed this faulty calendar to remain in use without objection.

sentences.zh: 論暉等情狀，已合科罪，方共飾非護短，不從正法。

translations.literal: Considering Hui and the others' circumstances, they already deserved punishment by law; yet they together embellished errors and shielded faults, not following correct law.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hui and his colleagues already deserved punishment; instead they embellished errors and shielded faults, defying proper procedure.

sentences.zh: 季才等附下罔上，義實難容。

translations.literal: Jicai and the others attached themselves below to deceive above—the righteousness of this was hard to tolerate."
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jicai and his colleagues deceived their superiors—conduct that could not be tolerated."

sentences.zh: 」於是暉等四人，元造詐者，並除名；

translations.literal: Thereupon Hui and the other four men, the original fabricators of fraud, were all stripped of their names;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hui and three others, the original authors of the faulty calendar, were stripped of rank;

sentences.zh: 季才等六人，容隱奸慝，俱解見任。

translations.literal: Jicai and the other six men, who concealed wickedness, were all dismissed from their current posts.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jicai and five others, who had concealed the fraud, were dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 胄玄所造曆法，付有司施行。

translations.literal: The calendar method created by Zhouxuan was entrusted to the relevant offices for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar was entrusted to the relevant offices for implementation.

sentences.zh: 擢拜胄玄為員外散騎侍郎，領太史令。

translations.literal: Zhouxuan was promoted and appointed Supernumerary Gentleman Attendant, concurrently Grand Astrologer.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhouxuan was promoted to Supernumerary Gentleman Attendant and appointed Grand Astrologer.

sentences.zh: 胄玄進袁充，互相引重，各擅一能，更為延譽。

translations.literal: Zhouxuan recommended Yuan Chong; they mutually promoted each other, each excelling in one skill, and further extended each other's reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhouxuan recommended Yuan Chong; they promoted each other, each claiming mastery in one area, and further burnished each other's reputations.

sentences.zh: 胄玄言充曆妙極前賢，充言胄玄曆術冠於今古。

translations.literal: Zhouxuan said Chong's calendar reached the subtle extreme of former sages; Chong said Zhouxuan's calendrical art topped all from ancient times to the present.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhouxuan declared Yuan Chong's calendar the finest since antiquity; Yuan Chong declared Zhang Zhouxuan's calendrical art unmatched in all history.

sentences.zh: 胄玄學祖沖之，兼傳其師法。

translations.literal: Zhouxuan studied Zu Chongzhi and also transmitted his master's methods.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhouxuan studied Zu Chongzhi and also transmitted his master's methods.

sentences.zh: 自茲厥後，克食頗中。

translations.literal: From this time forward, eclipse predictions largely hit the mark.
translations.idiomatic: From this point forward, eclipse predictions largely hit the mark.

sentences.zh: 其開皇十七年所行曆術，命冬至起虛五度。

translations.literal: The calendrical method used from Kaihuang 17 set winter solstice beginning at five degrees of xu.
translations.idiomatic: The calendar adopted in Kaihuang 17 set the winter solstice at the fifth degree of the Xu lodge.

sentences.zh: 後稍覺其疏，至大業四年劉焯卒後，乃敢改法，命起虛七度，諸法率更有增損，朔終義寧。

translations.literal: Later it was gradually felt to be coarse; by Daye 4, after Liu Chuo's death, he dared to change the method, setting the beginning at seven degrees of xu; the various methods were generally further added to and reduced, continuing until Yining.
translations.idiomatic: Later its imprecision became apparent; by Daye 4, after Liu Chuo's death, Zhang Zhouxuan revised the method to set the winter solstice at the seventh degree of Xu, with further adjustments to various parameters, continuing until the Yining era.

sentences.zh: 今錄戊辰年所定曆術著之於此雲。

translations.literal: Now the calendar method fixed in the wuchen year is recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: What follows records the calendar method fixed in the wuchen year.

sentences.zh: 自甲子元至大業四年戊辰，百四十二萬七千六百四十四年，算外。

translations.literal: From the jiazi origin to Daye 4, wuchen, one million four hundred twenty-seven thousand six hundred forty-four years, outside the calculation.
translations.idiomatic: From the jiazi origin to Daye 4 (wuchen): 1,427,644 years beyond the epoch.
